name: kilnspire-ledger
premise: The great central massif split this land into a rim of green coasts and one soot-blackened city that learned to eat stone. Kilnspire's forges supply nearly every beam, blade, and brick on the continent — but its terraces grow almost nothing, and its people are always three missed grain shipments from famine. The lowland cities whisper about a food cartel; Kilnspire whispers back about what happens when the ore stops flowing.

cities.name: Brinemark
cities.lore: A cold-water fishing republic on the northern shore, rich in salted cod and tidal mills. Proud, prosperous, and acutely aware that every roof beam in the city was bought from Kilnspire.

cities.name: Kilnspire
cities.lore: Carved into the eastern face of the massif, its foundries never cool and its granaries never fill. Kilnspire sells the world its bones and buys back its bread — and it never forgets a short delivery.

cities.name: Emberfall
cities.lore: Western highlanders who tapped the geothermal seams under their plateau and farm the misty valleys below. They light half the continent and own not a single quarry.

cities.name: Greyharrow
cities.lore: A southern breadbasket at the mountain's foot, running a modest quarry it insists is 'just for local use.' Everyone knows Greyharrow could undercut Kilnspire tomorrow — if it dared.

designNotes: The arena is built around a near-monopoly with a soft underbelly. Kilnspire is the only serious materials producer, so Brinemark and Emberfall must court it or starve for stone — but Kilnspire itself grows no food and must buy from Brinemark or Greyharrow, so its leverage is real but never safe. Greyharrow is the deliberate wildcard: its secondary materials output is too small to replace Kilnspire outright, but large enough to keep one defector alive, making it the kingmaker in any embargo. The natural fault lines: the three lowland cities can cartel food to bring Kilnspire to heel, but Greyharrow profits most from breaking that cartel; Kilnspire can divide-and-rule with materials pricing, but any overreach pushes its customers toward Greyharrow's quarry. At productionPerCapita 0.20 the world is tight — a two-front betrayal kills, so every threat has to be priced against the risk of mutual collapse. Expect shifting 3-vs-1 coalitions with Greyharrow deciding which side the '3' is on.
